## Contributors

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Dà-ānbān shǒuyì jīng* (T602) is a two-fascicle text of immense significance in early Chinese Buddhism — for centuries the principal Chinese exposition of *ānāpānasmṛti* (mindfulness of breathing) and the foundational text of the *chán* (*dhyāna*) movement of the Eastern Hàn 後漢 and Three Kingdoms. The transmitted text, however, is universally recognized in modern scholarship to be a heavily commentated composite, with Ān Shìgāo's underlying translation overlaid by interlinear and embedded commentary by [康僧會](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BA%B7%E5%83%A7%E6%9C%83) Kāng Sēnghuì (and possibly [支遁](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%94%AF%E9%81%81) Zhī Dùn) that has become inseparable from the root text.

**Abstract**

A composite-witness text that reflects the very earliest layer of *dhyāna* practice in China. Modern Jan Nattier (2008, 2014) and Stefano Zacchetti (2002, 2010) have shown that Kongō-ji 金剛寺 (Japan) preserves an alternative manuscript redaction without commentary that is much closer to Ān Shìgāo's translation; T602 should therefore be read as a hybrid commentary-text, not a pure Hàn translation. The bracket 148–170 CE corresponds to Ān Shìgāo's documented translation activity at Luòyáng under Hàn Huándì 漢桓帝.
